captions.detailed: This 3D model is a customizable nameplate designed for dual-color printing. It features a flat rectangular base plate with rounded corners and an angled support foot extending from the bottom rear to allow it to stand upright on a desk. The front of the plate contains a recessed border and a raised text nameplate insert, which can be printed separately and fitted together.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric name tag in OpenSCAD with a customizable text string, plate dimensions, and text height. Include an optional angled support foot extending from the back of the base plate, and structure the code so the text insert and the main backing plate can be rendered and printed as separate parts.
captions.factory: The design is split into two main modules: 'back' and 'label'. The base plate in 'back' is constructed by applying the hull() function over four thin cylinders translated to the corners, creating rounded edges. An optional support foot is appended using a cube rotated by 'Foot_angle' and translated to the bottom edge. The 'label' module uses write.scad to render the text, surrounded by a border created by subtracting a smaller hulled cylinder shape from a larger one. Depending on the 'part' parameter, a difference() operation subtracts the label from the back plate, or the label is rendered independently.
